title.narrative: {Consortium} Strengthening Food Security and Resilience through Integrated FSL, Health, Nutrition, and Protection services in Conflict-Affected East Darfur, Sudan

description.narrative: ltpgtThrough this project, Alight will collaborate with its partners—AAO, ZOA, AMVO, and WVI—to launch a comprehensive response that integrates Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL), Health, Nutrition, and Protection Services. This initiative will focus on the Sharia and Alferdous localities and aims to provide an integrated response for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host communities.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe situation in East Darfur reveals significant gaps in crop protection activities, and this project aims to address the current humanitarian needs. The targeted locality has been prioritized across all sectors, especially regarding food security and the general protection of farms during various cultivation stages. Our activities are aligned with the priorities established by relevant clusters. Alight and its partners will implement a comprehensive approach to its programming, ensuring that the targeted communities participate in both the implementation and evaluation processes. We will coordinate with local NGOs and UN agencies, primarily FAO and UNHCR, as well as line ministries and the crop protection committee, to provide timely assistance and ensure the safety of farms during cultivation and harvesting.ltbrgtAdditionally, the project aims to promote gender equality and women's empowerment, addressing the affected population's overall humanitarian needs and priorities. Alight will coordinate responses with local government and existing partners and participate in the cluster coordination system to enhance cooperation, reduce duplication, and deliver timely services to those in need.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtIn light of the significant humanitarian needs in Sudan, Alight has proposed a 12-month project. The objective is to strengthen food security and resilience through integrated FSL, Health, Nutrition, and Protection services in conflict-affected East Darfur. The project seeks to address the immediate needs of approximately 113,236 vulnerable individuals in Al Firdous and Sharia, including 36,182 women, 29,870 girls, 19,053 men, and 28,131 boys.lt/pgtltpgtHealth activities will encompass the provision of essential medical supplies, the establishment of mobile clinics, and the training of healthcare workers to ensure the delivery of primary healthcare. Special attention will be given to maternal and child health, vaccination campaigns, and the management of common diseases.lt/pgtltpgtNutrition efforts will target malnutrition through therapeutic and supplementary feeding programs for children as well as for pregnant and lactating women. Additionally, nutrition education sessions will enhance community knowledge and practices regarding healthy diets and infant feeding.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtProtection activities will focus on creating a safe environment by strengthening protection services and implementing community-based protection strategies to enhance resilience and safety.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtFSL initiatives aim to improve access to food and livelihood services by providing critical agricultural inputs, primarily seeds and tools. The project will also enhance farmers’ knowledge and skills in improved farming practices and create a supportive environment for better crop safety.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtBy addressing these essential needs, the project aims to improve the overall well-being of IDPs and host communities in Sharia and Alferdous, ensuring access to vital services and support during this crisis. Alight will implement Health, Nutrition, FSL, and Protection interventions, while AAO and ZOA will focus on FSL initiatives. AMVO will handle health and nutrition, and WVI will implement Health, Nutrition, and Protection services.lt/pgt
